title: terraform(private): reorganize GPU node pools state layout and split IAM/VPC modules
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: As customers adopt Private (VPC/on-prem) installs with GPU-backed workloads, we observed painful state churn when node pools were managed inline with cluster state. This PR refactors the Terraform layout to separate GPU node pool state into its own module and state file, splits IAM roles/policies into a dedicated module that can be composed by deployment type, and stabilizes VPC networking inputs to avoid unnecessary diffs during upgrades. The goals are: 1) enable zero-downtime node pool upgrades by allowing independent lifecycle and tainting; 2) provide clear IAM boundaries so Dedicated/Private can opt into least-privilege roles; 3) make state migration path explicit and reversible.

What changed (summary): reorganized modules/terraform state layout for private deployments, introduced modules/gpu-node-pool with its own backend configuration and locking logic, extracted modules/iam -> modules/iam/core and modules/iam/private (role separation), tightened modules/vpc input validation and added idempotent subnetwork handling, added a migration helper (scripts/migrate-gpu-state.sh) which automates a safe state move with checks and rollback, added integration tests for private cluster provisioning with GPU node pools, and updated examples and docs for upgrade/rollback steps.

Why this is safe: changes are additive - existing public hosted workflows are untouched. Private installer flows reference the new modules via the release tag in this PR. The migration script performs a terraform state mv with validation and an optional dry-run; CI runs the migration in a disposable test backend to validate procedure. We coordinated with SRE to ensure the migration is run during a maintenance window for customers on older layouts.

Upgrade notes / migration steps (short): 1) run scripts/migrate-gpu-state.sh --dry-run against your existing state backend to see planned moves; 2) schedule maintenance window if you have active GPU workloads; 3) run without --dry-run to perform the state mv; 4) apply the top-level private deployment plan which now references the gpu-node-pool module backend. Rollback: the migration script snapshots state (terraform state pull -> backup) and will attempt to move resources back if --rollback is provided.

Included tests and validation: terraform fmt/validate across modules, unit tests for the module input sanitizers (go test), an integration job that spins a private cluster in a disposable project and performs terraform apply/plan for node pool changes, and e2e smoke tests to confirm GPU nodes join and kubelet labels are correct.

References: Linear ENG-3120 (private infra state refactor), SUP-901 (customer migration request), design notes in docs/private/state-layout.md. Checklist: [x] tests added/updated, [x] migration script included, [x] docs updated, [x] reviewers + SRE notified, [x] CI green. This PR is expected to be merged via squash and backported to the 2026.02 release branch if needed.

release_notes: Private deployments: GPU node pool state split into a dedicated module and backend to enable independent upgrades without touching control-plane state.
IAM: roles and policies split to provide private/deployment-specific least-privilege configurations.
Migration: scripts/migrate-gpu-state.sh provided to safely move existing resources to the new state layout (dry-run and rollback supported).
notes_for_ops: Run migration script with --dry-run and validate plan before running in production.
Coordinate with SRE for maintenance window for clusters with active GPU workloads.
Back up terraform state before performing migration (terraform state pull > backup.tfstate).
